A read-only Redis cache service used by the Backend Service (web profile) that retrieves cached data without ever writing to or invalidating the cache.

## Key Components

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `ReadOnlyCacheService` | Spring `@Service("readOnlyCache")` extending `RedisCacheService`; active in the web/API profile |
| `put()` | No-op override — silently discards all write attempts |
| `invalidate()` | No-op override — silently discards all invalidation attempts |
| `get()` | Always returns the cached value, ignoring the `refreshInterval` parameter entirely |
| `getGitHubApiResponse()` | Returns a cached `JsonObject` for a GitHub API page; returns `Optional.empty()` on miss (never calls the supplier) |
| `getHttpResponse()` | Returns a cached contributor list for a filtered query; returns `Optional.empty()` on miss (never calls the supplier) |
| `getInsertTime()` | Returns `0L` — insert age is irrelevant in read-only mode |

## Usage Example

```java
// Injected via Spring qualifier in the Backend Service
@Qualifier("readOnlyCache")
private RedisCacheService cacheService;

// Reads succeed normally
Optional<List<Contributor>> contributors = cacheService.getHttpResponse(
    "chicago", null, "IL", null, "java", 50, () -> List.of()
);

// Writes are silently swallowed — no exception thrown
cacheService.put("/cache/path", "some-key", myObject); // no-op

// Supplier lambdas passed to getGitHubApiResponse / getHttpResponse
// are NEVER invoked in this implementation — cache misses return empty
Optional<JsonObject> page = cacheService.getGitHubApiResponse(
    city, "python", 1, () -> fetchFromGitHub() // never called
);
```

> **Design intent:** This service enforces a strict separation of concerns — the Backend Service reads from Redis while the Cache Updater microservice (port 8451) is the sole writer. Passing a supplier to `getGitHubApiResponse` or `getHttpResponse` is a no-op; the supplier is accepted for interface compatibility but never executed.
